initiative.title: MCP server for agent-driven analysis
initiative.summary: An exploreda MCP server lets an outside agent kick off a project from data or .eda files, build and revise views, and get DSL check, field, and reference feedback, with coverage growing toward everything a user can control.
initiative.next_action: Start M1: shared tool module, checker bundle, /mcp route, then the cold-agent proof.

sources.anchor: Request to create the MCP server initiative
sources.notes: Agent can create views and control anything the user can; kickoff by uploading data or .eda files; server reports useful info and DSL syntax checking.
Project folder format, guarded local server, ProjectFiles port, SSE file watching.
File server only; token and Host checks; codec and compiler run in the browser.
DSL checking and project loading already run in Node via registerAllCharts and readProjectFolder.
In-app agent with server-held credentials; distinct from an external MCP client.

claims.statement: An outside agent can start a project from data files or .eda text and get working views.
The MCP server returns actionable DSL feedback: parse and build problems with fixes, fields, and reference.
Coverage grows toward parity with everything a user can control.
claims.notes: Round 1: launch parity means saved state through files; live tab state later.

claims.statement: Agent output is ordinary project text a person can open and edit.
No model or credentials live in explorEDA for this initiative.
The agent connects to the running exploreda server over HTTP and joins the open session.
A stale agent write fails and the agent rereads.
Data kickoff covers local files, inline rows, and URL fetch; database sources follow database-adapters.
Launch without chart images; images are important and the main trigger for headless rendering.
The server writes a git-ignored .exploreda/server.json; an `exploreda mcp` helper reads it and relays to the running server, so the agent config is one fixed line.
Checks run in the server, loading the exploreda-dsl bundle lazily on the first MCP call.

answers.chart images: Launch without; note headless rendering is important and will likely help a lot
answers.connection: Join the running app (MCP over HTTP)
answers.data kickoff: Local files, inline rows, and URL fetch; MCP supports databases once database-adapters lands

shape.appetite: Launch-quality MCP endpoint on the running exploreda server with kickoff (files, rows, URL), feedback, and editing tools, plus docs and an example session.
shape.problem: An external agent has no checked, structured way to create and revise explorEDA analyses or learn why its DSL fails.
shape.recommended_shape: Project files as the control surface, served as an MCP endpoint on the running exploreda server: tools wrap the folder codec and exploreda-dsl check/fields/reference/describe, writes return check results with a stale-read guard, and the open tab updates through existing file watching. A git-ignored .exploreda/server.json plus an `exploreda mcp` relay helper gives agents one fixed config line; the checker bundle loads lazily on the first tool call.
success_moves: Reuse exploreda-dsl and readProjectFolder in Node, loaded lazily on the first MCP call, instead of a new compiler path.
Return the check result from every write so check-and-fix is one loop.
Use existing SSE file watching for live app updates instead of a browser bridge.
Guard writes with a read-version check so concurrent human edits are not overwritten.
Prove with a cold agent before adding finer edit tools.
Discovery file plus relay helper so per-run port and key never reach agent config.

first_proof.question: Can a cold agent reach a fully built analysis using only MCP tool results?
first_proof.artifact: check, fields, reference, and whole-file write_eda served from the running server over the shop example; a cold agent given a CSV and a dashboard request; count of check-fix rounds and problems lacking a usable fix.
first_proof.decision_rule: Within about five rounds: build the remaining tools on the file loop. Stalls on DSL syntax: put finer edit tools (add chart, set setting) ahead of whole-file writes.

rabbit_holes: Mirroring every UI gesture as a tool before agents need it.
A browser bridge before the file loop is proven.
Headless rendering pulled into launch scope.
URL fetch growing into a general connector; keep it to CSV/JSON with a size limit.

milestones.title: A cold agent builds a dashboard through four tools
milestones.outcome: check, fields, reference, write_eda served from /mcp on the running server; a cold agent reaches a built dashboard on the shop example.
milestones.proof: Vitest over memory files; exploreda-dsl output unchanged; recorded cold-agent transcript with round count.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: exploreda works unchanged; /mcp needs a pasted key.
milestones.rollback: Remove the /mcp route and checker bundle entry.

milestones.title: One fixed config line connects any agent
milestones.outcome: server.json discovery plus exploreda mcp stdio relay that starts a server when none runs.
milestones.proof: Restart and stale-key tests; real agent across a restart.
milestones.rollback: Drop the mcp subcommand and server.json writing.

milestones.title: The agent edits a project the way a person does
milestones.outcome: read/write/rename/delete/format/describe/project tools with a version guard; agent writes broadcast to the open tab.
milestones.proof: Conflict tests with editOutside; two-listener broadcast test; screenshots at three widths.

milestones.proof: Local fixture HTTP server tests for size, type, redirect, timeout.

history.event: Initiative created with intent brief and draft shape brief; status planned.
Question round 1 answered; shape moved from stdio to HTTP on the running server, URL fetch added, images and databases deferred.
Round 2 answered: discovery file + relay helper; lazy server-side checker. Shape marked current and plan-ready.
Implementation plan written: five milestones from a four-tool cold-agent proof to launch.
